sources: existing atomic corpse creation, loot, decay, and save/load paths

semantics.reservation_owner: persisted corpse LimitedItemReservationOwnerId; legacy/null records safely fall back to corpse CharacterId
semantics.counted_state: root and nested corpse-held items count toward the reservation owner when maximum_owned_quantity is projected
semantics.acquisition: creation, pickup, purchase, give, NPC transfer, and restore paths reject owner-limit overflow while a corpse reservation exists
semantics.loot: the transferred corpse quantity is excluded from its old reservation before destination-owner enforcement
semantics.release: recursive corpse decay removes reserved instances and releases counts atomically
semantics.rollback: failed acquisition leaves corpse, item, and owner state unchanged

assumptions: Exact Classic limited-item scope and corpse reservation rules are not yet decoded.
Only items with explicit maximum_owned_quantity metadata participate.
Account, party, guild, and world scopes remain inactive.
safe_fallback: Items without projected maximum_owned_quantity are unaffected; legacy corpse records use CharacterId only as a compatibility reservation identity.
tests: duplicate owner acquisition rejected while corpse holds limited item
nested corpse contents resolve through their root corpse
runtime_impact: Owner-scoped limited-item enforcement now spans active corpses and nested corpse containers.
character_save_impact: Corpse reservation owner persists with RuntimeCorpseState and legacy saves remain readable.
world_state_impact: Active corpse reservations participate in deterministic validation and release on cleanup.
